effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive synthesis and thematic study counts across 37 included studies (no pooled meta-analysis conducted). Note minor internal discrepancy in health challenge count between Abstract (n = 12) and Section 3.4.2 (n = 14, 38%).
effect_estimate.value: Across 37 included studies (25 countries), factors influencing choice of faecal sludge (FS) emptying method were accessibility to facilities/providers (n = 18, 49%), cost/affordability (n = 14, 38%), service quality (n = 13, 35%), and sludge thickness (n = 8, 22%). Challenges faced by FS emptiers comprised financial, technical, and institutional/regulatory challenges (n = 14, 38% each), health/safety hazards (n = 12 in abstract; n = 14, 38% in text), and social stigma/illegality (n = 8, 22%). Documented legal/administrative barriers included lengthy bureaucratic municipal procedures and untimeliness of city-corporation services pushing households toward informal manual emptiers; absent or poorly enforced FSM regulations and containment construction standards; costly permits/documents, disposal-site taxes, and unofficial fees/bribes; and criminalization of manual emptying. Improvement initiatives (n = 13, 35%)—public-private partnerships (n = 3) and NGO/CBO/donor/municipal programs (n = 10, 27%) using subsidies, equipment leasing, and scheduled desludging (e.g., 95% compliance in Marikina City, Philippines)—were constrained primarily by user affordability and emptiers' limited access to finance.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 4-10, Sections 3.3-3.5 & Figures 2-5

mechanism_certainty.comment: Secondary PRISMA-guided systematic review synthesizing thematic counts and narrative findings from 37 observational, practitioner, and case studies without primary empirical observation by the review authors or formal risk-of-bias appraisal of included primary studies; capped below 3 by systematic review design and coded 1 for documented descriptive associations and secondary accounts of institutional/administrative barriers.
